column1: # The libraries whose repository a build fetches with a credential. Every other library is fetched with none, which
# is what the builder's fetch-commit does by default and what the public enrollment build has always done: a row
# here, and nothing else, makes a build ask for a token. This is a list and not a rule about an account on purpose.
# Authenticating everything under one account would make every public build depend on the token service being up,
# and would change how the whole fleet fails for the sake of the few repositories below.
# For a library listed here, oss-verify check mints a token for that one build, read-only (contents and metadata) and
# narrowed to that one repository, and gives it to `docker build` as the BuildKit secret oss-verify-git-token. The
# project's Dockerfile must mount it on the fetch step, and oss-verify check refuses the build if it does not:
# oss-verify check equally refuses a project that is NOT listed here whose Dockerfile asks for that mount.
# The token comes from the command in OSS_VERIFY_GIT_TOKEN_COMMAND, else infra/github-read-token. It is never a
# stored credential, is never written into the image, a layer, the facts or the log, and no build has one unless its
# repository is a row here. docs/build-contract.md, "A private library", describes the whole path.
# The enrollment build in .github/workflows/build.yaml has no token command and must never be given one: it builds
# code from anyone. A library listed here is built on our own machines.
